709568.t: Probably from a Proto-Indo-European *h₃ligos (“indigent, small, needy, ill”). Compare Old Armenian աղքատ (ałkʻat, “poor, indigent”), Old Irish líach (“wretched”), Old Prussian licuts (“small”).

709597.t: From Proto-Hellenic *holwos, from Proto-Indo-European *solh₂wós, from *solh₂- (“whole”). Cognates include Sanskrit सर्व (sárva), Avestan 𐬵𐬀𐬎𐬭𐬬𐬀 (haurva), Latin salvus, sollus.

709555.t: From Proto-Hellenic *oktṓ, from Proto-Indo-European *oḱtṓw. Cognates include Sanskrit अष्ट (aṣṭa), Latin octō, and Old English eahta (English eight).

709516.t: From ϝοῖκος (woîkos), from Proto-Hellenic *wóikos, from Proto-Indo-European *wóyḱos (“settlement”).

709530.t: From Proto-Hellenic *wóinos (compare Mycenaean Greek 𐀺𐀜 (wo-no)), from Proto-Indo-European *wéyh₁ō; related to English wine, Latin vīnum, Old Armenian գինի (gini) etc.; according to the Oxford Latin Dictionary, "all probably from a common Mediterranean…

709517.t: Present passive participle of οἰκέω (oikéō, “I inhabit, dwell”). The noun use is an ellipsis of οἰκουμένη γῆ (oikouménē gê, “inhabited earth”).

709537.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₁eys-, used to form words denoting passion; see also Latin īra (“anger”), Lithuanian aistra (“violent passion”), Avestan 𐬀𐬉𐬴𐬨𐬀 (aēṣ̌ma, “anger”).

709509.t: From οἰκοδόμος (oikodómos, “builder, architect”) + -έω (-éō, denominative verbal suffix).

709535.t: From ὅς (hós, relative pronoun) + -ιος (-ios, adjectival suffix).

709534.t: From earlier ὀΐομαι (oī̈́omai) and *ὀϝίομαι (*owī́omai), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ew- (“perceive”).

709539.t: Mediopassive form (with perfective meaning?) to Ancient Greek οἰχνέω (oikhnéō, “to go, come, walk, approach”), both connected to Armenian and Tocharian verbal forms (with meanings such as Old Armenian իջանեմ (iǰanem, “to come down”) and Tocharian B yku…

709584.t: From the Greek descendant of Proto-Indo-European *h₃elh₁- (“destroy”) + -νυμι (-nūmĭ), with assimilation of *-λν- (*-ln-) to -λλ- (-ll-). Compare Latin ab-oleō, which may be related.

709563.t: From Proto-Hellenic *óletʰros, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃elh₁dʰros, from *h₃elh₁- (“to destroy”). Cognate with ὄλλυμι (óllūmĭ).

709565.t: According to Beekes, the term derives from the root Proto-Indo-European *h₃elh₁- with a k-enlargement. For comparison, see terms such as ἐρύκω (erúkō).

709558.t: Furnée connects ὄλπα (ólpa, “kind of food”). According to Beekes, if the gloss is cognate, then it must be Pre-Greek.

709514.t: From οἶκος (oîkos, “house, home, estate”) + νόμος (nómos, “law, rule, authority”), equivalent to οἶκος (oîkos) + νέμω (némō) + -ος (-os).

709545.t: Explanation debated. Because of the comparable formation in υἱωνός (huiōnós, “grandson”) from υἱός (huiós, “son”), it is probably best derived from a nominal basis.

709507.t: οἶκος (oîkos, “home”) + -ίζω (-ízō, “a suffix forming a verb from a noun”)

709593.t: Onomatopoeic reduplicated formation, with the same ending of ἰύζω (iúzō, “to shout, yell”).

709550.t: From ὀκνέω (oknéō, “to shrink, hesitate”) + -ρός (-rós, adjective suffix).

709503.t: From οἰκέω (oikéō, “inhabit, dwell”) + -τός (-tós, “A suffix creating verbal adjectives of possibility, either active or passive”)

709599.t: From ὅλος (hólos, “whole”) + an element *σχερός (*skherós, “row”), the latter formed from a zero-grade of Proto-Indo-European *seǵʰ- (“to hold, have”), + -ής (-ḗs). See also ἐπισχερώ (episkherṓ, “in a row”).
